transcript:
Meeting header:
2026-06-03 14:00 UTC | Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maria Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jesse Lopez (CSM); Eli Navarro (Quantaco Head of ML), Priya Singh (SRE), Carlos Mendes (CTO), Ana Torres (Data Eng)

Summary (auto): quick recap of last week's POC runs focused on tokens/sec per dollar and where caching/batching gave us wins; aligned on next live benchmark and deliverables.

00:00 Maria Chen: okay hey everyone, um, quick roll call 1 can you all hear me?
00:06 Eli Navarro: yep loud and clear, thanks Maria
00:10 Samir Patel: hey team, Samir here 1 I'm gonna walk through the cost numbers from today's runs and the tradeoffs we saw
00:18 Priya Singh: hi all, Priya here 1 I have a quick question on caching TTLs later
00:22 Maria Chen: great, goal is to validate tokens per dollar and decide if we start a dedicated pilot next week. Samir take it away

02:05 Samir Patel: alright so we ran the three main profiles: hosted baseline (gpt-like 7B open), quantized 4-bit variant, and a ded-optimized variant on a smaller dedicated pool. numbers are rough  transcription artifact: I may say tps instead of tokens per second.
02:20 Samir Patel: hosted baseline average was about 420 tokens/sec across mixed prompts at 16k context, cost came to roughly $0.014 per 1k tokens (this is after our runtime-level batching/cold-start amortization).
03:04 Samir Patel: the quantized 4-bit gave us about 680 tokens/sec and cost down to ~ $0.009 per 1k tokens  roughly 35% cost improvement vs baseline, though we did see slightly higher tail latency on long sequences.
04:00 Samir Patel: dedicated pool at comparable RPS, with autoscale set conservatively, we saw 900 tokens/sec and modeled cost at about $0.0065 per 1k tokens  that's tokens/sec per dollar improvement but remember committed pricing and infra amortization assumptions apply.
04:35 Carlos Mendes: wait when you say cost per 1k tokens how are you counting cache hits? Are cache hits zeroed out?
04:45 Samir Patel: good Q  in these runs we reported net tokens billed (post-prefix caching). separate metric 'raw tokens' we logged too. the caching layer shaved off about 22% on average for our set because a lot of prompts had identical prefixes  that's the measured savings for default TTL 5m.
05:20 Ana Torres: 22% seems optimistic for our workload  most of our prompts are slightly different, are you seeing similar on our prompt sample?
05:28 Samir Patel: on Quantaco's sample the median was 18% savings, mean 22% driven by a small subset of high repetition. we can provide a per-prompt histogram after the call.
06:10 Eli Navarro: okay and batching? we worry about latency  our product needs sub-200ms p50 for interactive use
06:20 Samir Patel: yes  we tested three batching windows: 0ms (no batch), 30ms, 80ms. 30ms increased throughput ~15% with p50 unaffected, p95 rose from 160ms to 210ms on some long-context blends. 80ms pushed throughput ~40% but p50 climbed to ~220ms and p95 to ~450ms, so it's a tradeoff.
07:05 Priya Singh: interesting  what about adaptive batching? can Redwood do dynamic batch windows based on current latency?
07:12 Samir Patel: we have adaptive batching heuristics in the runtime, yes  you can set target p50 and we tune batch window up to configured max. that gave us middle-ground in tests: throughput +25% with p95 ~260ms.
07:36 Carlos Mendes: how about prefix vs KV cache? which one gave the biggest ROI?
07:43 Samir Patel: prefix (shared request prefix) gave quick wins for repeated prompts  KV cache for KV-cacheable LLM workloads gave more for multi-turn chat where history re-usage is big. for your use-case (mostly single-shot with repeated templates) prefix wins: ~12-22% savings; KV not as applicable unless you reuse long cached keys per user.
08:15 Maria Chen: quick note on quantization: we recommended the 4-bit profile for cost, but if you need strict SLO we can do mixed approach where critical routes use fp16 and bulk inference uses 4-bit. that usually nets best cost/latency balance.
09:00 Eli Navarro: do you have numbers for quality/accuracy regression when moving to 4-bit? we can't afford hallucination spikes
09:10 Samir Patel: in our eval set we saw negligible quality delta for the small set of generation tasks (BLEU-like/ROUGE proxies)  less than 1.5% metric drift, but we flagged a couple prompt patterns where the logits change enough that we suggest running targeted evals. we'll share the eval artifacts.
09:55 Priya Singh: on the security side, if we go dedicated we need KMS integration and audit logs for each token call  is that standard?
10:03 Maria Chen: yes, Dedicated and Private support KMS/HSM and per-request audit logs. we also have SOC 2 and ISO docs  I'll attach the package.
10:20 Carlos Mendes: any egress costs we should model for dedicated? network is a concern for us
10:27 Samir Patel: egress is external cloud egress  in-datacenter it's negligible. for the dedicated pricing model we included a line item for expected egress; we'll make it explicit in the worksheet.
11:00 Eli Navarro: can we talk about tokens/sec per dollar metric? I want a single row we can show execs
11:06 Samir Patel: yes suggested KPI: tokens/sec per $1000 per hour or tokens per dollar normalized by active GPU hours. today's rough numbers: hosted baseline ~30k tokens per dollar (norming by our internal calc), quantized ~46k tokens per dollar, dedicated ~68k tokens per dollar  again depends on commit and util.
11:35 Ana Torres: those look good but what's the sensitivity if we go from 50% to 80% cache hit rate?
11:42 Samir Patel: good sensitivity: at 80% hit rate savings jump a lot  extrapolating from our profile it takes tokens per dollar for dedicated from 68k to ~92k; hosted goes from 30k to ~43k. so caching multiplicatively helps dedicated more because infra is already amortized.
12:20 Priya Singh: any drawbacks for our tail-latency? high cache hits could mean cache thundering?
12:27 Samir Patel: we mitigate thundering with jittered TTL and lock-free cache warming; still need to plan for warm-up phases. for multi-tenant hosted we use rate-limiting per-key to avoid stampedes.
13:05 Carlos Mendes: on booking dedicated, what's the minimum commit look like? and how does it affect unit economics?
13:12 Maria Chen: commitments are flexible, but most pilots start with a 3-month reserved pool sized for peak concurrency; discounts apply and auto-scale handles bursts. longer commits improve the unit price because you're amortizing infra. we'll share modeled scenarios in the cost worksheet.
13:45 Eli Navarro: can Redwood run a dedicated benchmark for us with our prompt set? we'd like to see end-to-end cost including cache behaviour
13:51 Samir Patel: yes  proposed next live run: 5M tokens spread over 24 hours with your sample set, dedicated config with 30ms adaptive batching and prefix cache TTL 5m. we'll export raw tokens, billed tokens, latencies.
14:08 Maria Chen: timelineSamir will run it early next week, Maria will send cost model and pricing, Quantaco provides final prompt set and SLO targets.

15:20 Jesse Lopez: small ops note  if the dedicated test looks good we'll schedule on-prem validation; Priya can we sync infra requirements after this?
15:30 Priya Singh: yes I'll prepare network and KMS constraints doc and share via email.

16:00 Maria Chen: great, quick recap of agreed benchmarks and deliverables then close
16:10 Eli Navarro: thanks everyone, appreciate the data  talk soon

End of transcript
